question.text: Which things can weaken your driving, and who is responsible for knowing when you are not fit to drive?

answer.text: Alcohol, drugs, even medicine, and being tired can all weaken your driving, and you are the one responsible for knowing when you are not fit to drive.

teaching.text: The list is wider than alcohol: drugs, medicine and simple tiredness can all weaken driving, and the duty to judge your fitness stays with you. Remember: your fitness, your responsibility.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol, drugs, even medicine, and being tired can all weaken your driving, and you are the one responsible for knowing when you are not fit to drive.

question.text: If you plan to drink, what should you do with your car keys, and why?

answer.text: Even a little alcohol may affect your driving, so if you plan to drink, hand the keys to someone who has not been drinking.

teaching.text: The advice works before the first drink: plan for someone who has not been drinking to drive. Remember: drinking? hand over keys.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even a little alcohol may affect your driving, so if you plan to drink, hand the keys to someone who has not been drinking.

question.text: Besides weakening your driving directly, what other effects can alcohol cause?

answer.text: Alcohol can also cause drowsiness, weaker concentration and attention, poorer coordination and comprehension, and worse decisions.

teaching.text: Each effect on this list, from drowsiness to worse decisions, is one more way alcohol can leave you unfit to drive. Remember: drowsy, unfocused, clumsy, worse decisions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alcohol can also cause drowsiness, weaker concentration and attention, poorer coordination and comprehension, and worse decisions.

question.text: How much can one drink, or two drinks, affect your driving?

answer.text: Even one drink will probably affect your driving, and in many cases two drinks could put you over the legal limit.

teaching.text: Notice the wording: one drink probably affects you, and two could be enough in many cases to cross the legal limit. Remember: one probably, two possibly over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even one drink will probably affect your driving, and in many cases two drinks could put you over the legal limit.

question.text: At what BAC is it illegal to drive for most drivers, for commercial vehicle drivers and for drivers under twenty-one?

answer.text: It is illegal to drive with a BAC of zero point zero eight percent or more, with zero point zero four percent for commercial vehicle drivers and zero point zero two percent for drivers under twenty-one.

teaching.text: The number goes down as the driver changes: most drivers, then commercial vehicle drivers, then drivers under twenty-one. Remember: eight, four, two by driver.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: It is illegal to drive with a BAC of zero point zero eight percent or more, with zero point zero four percent for commercial vehicle drivers and zero point zero two percent for drivers under twenty-one.

question.text: Why is the legal BAC limit not the same number for every driver?

answer.text: The legal BAC limit depends on the driver: zero point zero eight percent for most drivers, zero point zero four percent for commercial vehicle drivers, and zero point zero two percent for drivers under twenty-one.

teaching.text: Before judging a BAC reading, identify the driver, because the same reading can be legal for one driver and illegal for another. Remember: match the limit to driver.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The legal BAC limit depends on the driver: zero point zero eight percent for most drivers, zero point zero four percent for commercial vehicle drivers, and zero point zero two percent for drivers under twenty-one.

question.text: In Missouri, which substances can lead to a DWI charge if they impair your driving?

answer.text: In Missouri you can be charged with DWI for driving impaired by alcohol, illegal drugs, prescription medicine, over-the-counter medicine, or any mix of them.

teaching.text: DWI is about impairment, not just alcohol, so prescription and over-the-counter medicines count as much as illegal drugs. Remember: any impairing substance counts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In Missouri you can be charged with DWI for driving impaired by alcohol, illegal drugs, prescription medicine, over-the-counter medicine, or any mix of them.

question.text: Does Missouri law treat prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drugs differently, and do DWI penalties change when drugs caused the impairment?

answer.text: Missouri law does not separate prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drugs, and DWI penalties are the same whether alcohol or drugs caused the impairment.

teaching.text: A prescription does not soften the outcome; the law treats drug impairment the same as alcohol impairment. Remember: drugs or alcohol, same penalties.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Missouri law does not separate prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drugs, and DWI penalties are the same whether alcohol or drugs caused the impairment.

question.text: What field tests may an officer who suspects drinking ask you to do, and what are they for?

answer.text: An officer who suspects drinking may ask you to do field tests such as walking heel to toe or balancing on one leg, which help the officer decide whether to arrest you.

teaching.text: Field tests come before any arrest and guide that decision; the BAC level comes later from the chemical test. Remember: heel to toe, one leg.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An officer who suspects drinking may ask you to do field tests such as walking heel to toe or balancing on one leg, which help the officer decide whether to arrest you.

question.text: After an arrest, how is the alcohol in your body measured, and what is the result called?

answer.text: After an arrest, a chemical test of your breath, blood or urine gives your Blood Alcohol Content, called the BAC level.

teaching.text: The chemical test follows the arrest, and its result is the BAC level that the limits are measured against. Remember: breath, blood or urine.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After an arrest, a chemical test of your breath, blood or urine gives your Blood Alcohol Content, called the BAC level.

question.text: What happens to your license if you refuse a chemical test of your BAC when stopped by an officer?

answer.text: If you refuse a chemical test of your BAC when stopped by an officer, your license is taken away for one year.

teaching.text: Refusal is not a way around the test; it brings its own one-year loss of the license. Remember: refuse the test, lose a year.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you refuse a chemical test of your BAC when stopped by an officer, your license is taken away for one year.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: refuse the test, lose a year

question.text: In how many separate ways can Missouri act against an impaired driver, and what are they called?

answer.text: Missouri can act against an impaired driver in two separate ways, administrative actions and court-convicted actions, and each has its own penalties.

teaching.text: Keep the two tracks apart, because each one sets its own penalties. Remember: two tracks, two sets of penalties.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Missouri can act against an impaired driver in two separate ways, administrative actions and court-convicted actions, and each has its own penalties.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: two tracks, two sets of penalties

question.text: What does the officer do when your test shows a BAC at or above the limit, or the lower limit for a minor?

answer.text: If your BAC is.eight percent or more, or.two percent or more for a minor, the officer takes your license and gives you a notice that it will be suspended or revoked after fifteen days.

teaching.text: On the administrative track, the officer takes the license at the scene of the failed test, and the notice sets the fifteen-day countdown. Remember: license taken, notice served.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your BAC is.eight percent or more, or.two percent or more for a minor, the officer takes your license and gives you a notice that it will be suspended or revoked after fifteen days.

question.text: What may the notice given after a failed BAC test include, and what does it let you request?

answer.text: That notice may include a fifteen-day driving permit if the officer marks it, and it lets you ask for a hearing or, if eligible, an immediate ninety-day Restricted Driving Privilege.

teaching.text: The permit depends on the officer marking the notice, while the hearing or the restricted privilege depends on you asking for it. Remember: permit, hearing or restricted privilege.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: That notice may include a fifteen-day driving permit if the officer marks it, and it lets you ask for a hearing or, if eligible, an immediate ninety-day Restricted Driving Privilege.

question.text: If you are granted a hearing, until when may you keep driving legally?

answer.text: If you are granted a hearing, you may keep driving legally until fifteen days after the decision is mailed to you.

teaching.text: A granted hearing shifts the deadline: driving stays legal until fifteen days after the mailed decision. Remember: drive until decision plus fifteen.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you are granted a hearing, you may keep driving legally until fifteen days after the decision is mailed to you.

question.text: What two different fifteen-day periods appear on the arrest notice page?

answer.text: Two different fifteen-day periods appear on the arrest notice page: the license is lost fifteen days after the notice, and with a hearing you may drive until fifteen days after the decision is mailed.

teaching.text: Same length, different starting events: one period counts from the notice and the other from the mailed hearing decision. Remember: after notice, after decision.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Two different fifteen-day periods appear on the arrest notice page: the license is lost fifteen days after the notice, and with a hearing you may drive until fifteen days after the decision is mailed.

question.text: On the administrative chart, what does a first offense bring, and what does a second offense within five years bring?

answer.text: On the administrative chart, a first offense brings a license suspension, and a second offense within a five-year period brings a one-year license revocation.

teaching.text: The chart has two levels, and the second one depends on the offense falling within a five-year period. Remember: suspend first, revoke second.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On the administrative chart, a first offense brings a license suspension, and a second offense within a five-year period brings a one-year license revocation.

question.text: What does an asterisk beside an administrative chart entry require before reinstatement?

answer.text: Administrative entries marked with an asterisk require an Ignition Interlock Device to be installed before the license is reinstated.

teaching.text: For an asterisk entry, time alone does not bring the license back; the interlock has to be installed first. Remember: asterisk means interlock first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Administrative entries marked with an asterisk require an Ignition Interlock Device to be installed before the license is reinstated.

question.text: If a judge finds you guilty of DWI or of a BAC at the limit, when must you stop driving and how are you told?

answer.text: If a judge finds you guilty of DWI or of a BAC of.eight percent or more, you can no longer drive legally once the ticket reaches the Department, and you are told by mail when to stop.

teaching.text: After a court guilty finding, the stop date comes by mail once the ticket reaches the Department, not from the officer's notice. Remember: ticket arrives, letter tells you.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a judge finds you guilty of DWI or of a BAC of.eight percent or more, you can no longer drive legally once the ticket reaches the Department, and you are told by mail when to stop.

question.text: After a court conviction, what decides whether your license is suspended, revoked or denied, and what is added to your record?

answer.text: After a court conviction, your license is suspended, revoked or denied depending on your past driving record, and points are added to that record.

teaching.text: Two things follow a court conviction: a license action shaped by your past record, and new points on that same record. Remember: record decides, points added.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a court conviction, your license is suspended, revoked or denied depending on your past driving record, and points are added to that record.

question.text: What happens to the license after a first court-convicted offense, and what restricted privilege may you qualify for?

answer.text: For a first court-convicted offense the license is suspended for ninety days, and you may qualify for a ninety-day or sixty-day Restricted Driving Privilege.

teaching.text: The ninety-day figure appears twice here, as the suspension and as one of the two privilege lengths, so keep them apart. Remember: first: ninety-day suspension.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a first court-convicted offense the license is suspended for ninety days, and you may qualify for a ninety-day or sixty-day Restricted Driving Privilege.

question.text: What does a second court-convicted offense bring, and what changes if it comes within five years?

answer.text: A second court-convicted offense brings a one-year revocation, while a second offense within five years brings a five-year license denial.

teaching.text: The five-year window is the switch: outside it a second court offense is a revocation, inside it a five-year denial. Remember: second: revoke, or five-year denial.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A second court-convicted offense brings a one-year revocation, while a second offense within five years brings a five-year license denial.

question.text: What does a third court-convicted offense, or any later one, bring?

answer.text: A third court-convicted offense, and any later one, brings a ten-year license denial.

teaching.text: At the top of the court ladder, the denial grows from five years to ten. Remember: third and up: ten-year denial.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A third court-convicted offense, and any later one, brings a ten-year license denial.

question.text: Which BAC convictions can be counted toward a five-year license denial?

answer.text: Only a BAC conviction dated August twenty-eight, two thousand nine or later can be counted toward a five-year license denial.

teaching.text: The date of the conviction matters: an earlier BAC conviction cannot be counted toward the five-year denial. Remember: only convictions after the cutoff.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only a BAC conviction dated August twenty-eight, two thousand nine or later can be counted toward a five-year license denial.

question.text: What can being found guilty of drinking or using drugs while driving in Missouri bring?

answer.text: Being found guilty of drinking or using drugs while driving in Missouri can bring a fine, a lost license, and even jail.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Being found guilty of drinking or using drugs while driving in Missouri can bring a fine, a lost license, and even jail.

question.text: What penalties may you face if you injure or kill someone while driving after drinking or using drugs?

answer.text: If you injure or kill someone while driving after drinking or using drugs, you may face two to seven years in jail, a five thousand dollars fine, and or or losing your license for five years.

teaching.text: Harming someone carries its own penalty, separate from the conviction ladder, so check whether anyone was hurt. Remember: harm someone: jail, fine, license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you injure or kill someone while driving after drinking or using drugs, you may face two to seven years in jail, a five thousand dollars fine, and or or losing your license for five years.

question.text: What jail time and fine can a first DWI or BAC conviction mean?

answer.text: A first DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to six months in jail and a fine of up to five hundred dollars.

teaching.text: These are upper limits, written as up to, for the first rung of the ladder. Remember: first: six months, five hundred.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A first DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to six months in jail and a fine of up to five hundred dollars.

question.text: How does the effects page restate the DWI punishment?

answer.text: The effects page restates the DWI punishment as up to six months in prison, a fine of up to five hundred, dollars and loss of driving privileges.

teaching.text: The effects page and the penalty chart agree on the first-conviction limits, and the effects page adds the loss of driving privileges. Remember: prison, fine, lost privileges.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The effects page restates the DWI punishment as up to six months in prison, a fine of up to five hundred, dollars and loss of driving privileges.

question.text: What jail time and fine can a second DWI or BAC conviction mean?

answer.text: A second DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to one year in jail and a fine of up to one thousand dollars.

teaching.text: Both limits grow at the second conviction, jail to a year and the fine to one thousand dollars. Remember: second: one year, one thousand.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A second DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to one year in jail and a fine of up to one thousand dollars.

question.text: What jail time and fine can a third DWI or BAC conviction mean?

answer.text: A third DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to four years in jail and a fine of up to five thousand dollars.

teaching.text: The fine limit reaches five thousand dollars here and stays there for the fourth conviction. Remember: third: four years, five thousand.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A third DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to four years in jail and a fine of up to five thousand dollars.

question.text: What jail time and fine can a fourth DWI or BAC conviction mean?

answer.text: A fourth DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to seven years in jail and a fine of up to five thousand dollars.

teaching.text: Only the jail limit separates the fourth conviction from the third, since the fine limit is the same. Remember: fourth: seven years, five thousand.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A fourth DWI or BAC conviction can mean up to seven years in jail and a fine of up to five thousand dollars.

question.text: What range of jail time can a fifth DWI or BAC offense mean?

answer.text: A fifth DWI or BAC offense can mean between five and fifteen years in jail.

teaching.text: The fifth offense is written as a range with a starting point, not just an upper limit. Remember: fifth: five to fifteen years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A fifth DWI or BAC offense can mean between five and fifteen years in jail.

question.text: Who is it illegal for to possess or buy alcohol in Missouri?

answer.text: It is illegal for anyone under twenty-one to possess or buy alcohol in Missouri.

teaching.text: This is the base rule that the young-driver laws build on, and it covers anyone under twenty-one, driver or not. Remember: under twenty-one: no alcohol.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: It is illegal for anyone under twenty-one to possess or buy alcohol in Missouri.

question.text: Under the Abuse and Lose Law, what can happen to a driver younger than twenty-one, and for which offenses?

question.text: Under Abuse and Lose, what can happen to a driver under eighteen who has or uses alcohol and is charged with a second offense?

answer.text: A driver under eighteen who has or uses alcohol and is charged with a second offense can also lose the license for ninety days under Abuse and Lose.

question.text: How does the Abuse and Lose license loss differ for a driver under twenty-one and a driver twenty-one or older with drugs?

question.text: For which acts can a state court suspend or revoke the license of someone older than fifteen and under twenty-one?

question.text: For a young person, how does drinking liquor relate to possessing it?

answer.text: For a young person, drinking liquor counts as possessing it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a young person, drinking liquor counts as possessing it.

question.text: How do Minor in Possession penalties change with each offense?

question.text: What must you do after a Minor in Possession action, and what more after a one-year revocation?

question.text: How does a first Minor in Possession suspension compare with the Abuse and Lose loss?

answer.text: A first Minor in Possession offense brings a thirty-day suspension, which is shorter than the ninety-day loss under Abuse and Lose.

question.text: What three steps get you reinstated after an intoxication-related offense?

question.text: What must a driver facing DWI or BAC consequences file, with whom, and how is it most often done?

question.text: Who must run an ignition interlock device after reinstatement, on which vehicles, and for at least how long?

answer.text: A court conviction for failing to install a required interlock revokes your driving privilege for one year, and a second offense takes it away for five years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A court conviction for failing to install a required interlock revokes your driving privilege for one year, and a second offense takes it away for five years.

question.text: Which two penalties both cost one year of driving privilege?

answer.text: Refusing a chemical test and being convicted of not installing a required interlock both cost one year of driving privilege.

teaching.text: Two different actions end with the same one-year loss, which is why they are easy to mix up with other lengths. Remember: refuse or skip interlock: year.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Refusing a chemical test and being convicted of not installing a required interlock both cost one year of driving privilege.

question.text: Can medicines taken as directed impair driving, and what should you do about it?

answer.text: All medicines, prescription or over-the-counter, can impair driving even when taken as directed, so ask your doctor or pharmacist and read the warning label.

teaching.text: Taking a medicine as directed does not make it safe for driving, which is why the guide sends you to your doctor, pharmacist and label. Remember: ask, and read the label.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: All medicines, prescription or over-the-counter, can impair driving even when taken as directed, so ask your doctor or pharmacist and read the warning label.

question.text: How can cold and allergy medicines bought over the counter affect your driving?

answer.text: Cold and allergy medicines bought over the counter can make you drowsy and hurt your driving.

teaching.text: Buying a medicine off the shelf does not make it harmless behind the wheel. Remember: cold pills can cause drowsiness.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Cold and allergy medicines bought over the counter can make you drowsy and hurt your driving.

question.text: How do pep pills, uppers and diet pills affect a driver, first and later on?

answer.text: Pep pills, uppers and diet pills may make a driver more alert for a short time but later can cause nervousness, dizziness, poor concentration and vision problems.

teaching.text: The alert feeling is the short part; the problems that follow are the ones that weaken driving. Remember: alert now, impaired later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pep pills, uppers and diet pills may make a driver more alert for a short time but later can cause nervousness, dizziness, poor concentration and vision problems.

question.text: What should you do about a drug whose label warns of drowsiness or dizziness before you drive?

answer.text: Do not take any drug whose label warns that it may cause drowsiness or dizziness before you drive.

teaching.text: The rule is firm: with that warning on the label, you do not take the drug before driving. Remember: warning label means skip it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not take any drug whose label warns that it may cause drowsiness or dizziness before you drive.

question.text: Why should you not take a medicine prescribed for someone else, and when may you mix medicines?

answer.text: Taking a medicine prescribed for someone else is both dangerous and illegal, and you should not mix medicines unless your doctor tells you to.

teaching.text: Someone else's prescription is off limits entirely, while mixing your own medicines needs your doctor's instruction. Remember: not yours, not allowed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Taking a medicine prescribed for someone else is both dangerous and illegal, and you should not mix medicines unless your doctor tells you to.

question.text: Why should you never combine alcohol with any medicine?

answer.text: Never combine alcohol with any medicine, because many drugs have unexpected side effects when taken with alcohol.

teaching.text: The alcohol rule covers any medicine, prescription or not. Remember: never mix alcohol and medicine.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never combine alcohol with any medicine, because many drugs have unexpected side effects when taken with alcohol.

question.text: Where does marijuana rank among drugs cited in car crashes?

answer.text: Marijuana is the drug cited second most often in car crashes, after alcohol.

teaching.text: Only alcohol is cited more often than marijuana in car crashes. Remember: second only to alcohol.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Marijuana is the drug cited second most often in car crashes, after alcohol.

question.text: Since Missouri voters approved medical marijuana, is driving under its influence legal or safe?

answer.text: Missouri voters approved medical marijuana effective in two thousand twenty, yet driving under its influence is never legal or safe.

teaching.text: Approval for medical use is not permission to drive impaired. Remember: medical still means never drive.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Missouri voters approved medical marijuana effective in two thousand twenty, yet driving under its influence is never legal or safe.

question.text: How can marijuana affect a driver, and what do studies link it to?

answer.text: Marijuana can impair thinking, judgment of time and distance, and coordination, and studies link it to more lane weaving and slower reactions.

teaching.text: The effects reach both the mind and the vehicle: thinking and judgment, and weaving and slower reactions. Remember: weaving and slower reactions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Marijuana can impair thinking, judgment of time and distance, and coordination, and studies link it to more lane weaving and slower reactions.

question.text: How impaired were drivers who used alcohol together with marijuana, compared with marijuana alone?

answer.text: Drivers who used alcohol together with marijuana were even more impaired, with still more lane weaving, than with marijuana alone.

teaching.text: Combining the two is worse than marijuana alone, not a wash. Remember: mixing means even more weaving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers who used alcohol together with marijuana were even more impaired, with still more lane weaving, than with marijuana alone.

question.text: What is a substance use disorder?

answer.text: A substance use disorder is repeated alcohol or drug use that causes serious problems such as health issues, disability, or failing duties at work, school or home.

teaching.text: The disorder is about a pattern of repeated use that causes serious problems, not a single use. Remember: repeated use, serious problems.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A substance use disorder is repeated alcohol or drug use that causes serious problems such as health issues, disability, or failing duties at work, school or home.

question.text: What risk do people with a substance use disorder face in a motor vehicle?

answer.text: People with a substance use disorder are at greater risk of hurting themselves or others in a motor vehicle crash.

teaching.text: The risk is to the person with the disorder and to others on the road. Remember: greater crash risk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: People with a substance use disorder are at greater risk of hurting themselves or others in a motor vehicle crash.

question.text: Where can someone get help for a substance use disorder, and what is that help like?

answer.text: Help for a substance use disorder is available through the free, confidential SAMHSA National Helpline, open around the clock every day of the year.

teaching.text: Help costs nothing, stays confidential and is open at any hour of any day. Remember: free, confidential, always open.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Help for a substance use disorder is available through the free, confidential SAMHSA National Helpline, open around the clock every day of the year.

question.text: Why is early use one of the strongest predictors of addiction?

answer.text: Early use is one of the strongest predictors of addiction, because a young brain that is still developing can be damaged faster and more severely than an adult brain.

teaching.text: A brain that is still developing can be damaged faster and more severely, which is why early use matters. Remember: young brains damage faster.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Early use is one of the strongest predictors of addiction, because a young brain that is still developing can be damaged faster and more severely than an adult brain.
